R0140.title: Membership / Subscription Abuse
R0140.definition: Repeatedly obtaining free benefits by exploiting trial period and subscription mechanism loopholes, or illegally obtaining and distributing paid benefits through sharing or reselling membership accounts.
R0140.description: Membership/subscription abuse involves fraud targeting platform membership systems and subscription services. Main patterns include: (1) Trial period abuse: repeatedly registering new accounts to obtain free trial benefits, abandoning accounts when they expire and re-registering. (2) Benefit sharing: sharing personal membership account credentials with multiple people beyond the authorized scope. (3) Membership reselling: bulk-registering or stealing membership accounts and reselling them at low prices on third-party platforms. (4) Refund benefit retention: activating membership, using benefits, then canceling the subscription through refund mechanisms while retaining already-obtained benefits (such as downloaded content). (5) Downgrade arbitrage: concentrating use of high-tier benefits during the grace period before immediately downgrading. (6) Family plan abuse: adding non-family members to family sharing plans to obtain membership benefits at low cost.
R0140.influence: Causes platform membership revenue losses, degrades paid user experience, and dilutes the value of the membership system.

observables: The same membership account logs in concurrently from multiple distant regions or heterogeneous devices within a short window, exceeding household usage patterns
Newly registered accounts concentrate benefit usage as the trial period nears expiry, then abandon the account and re-activate a trial with a new account
Bulk listings reselling the platform's membership accounts at low prices appear on third-party platforms, with account credentials frequently changed
Membership benefits of high value are used shortly after activation, followed by a refund to cancel the subscription while retaining downloaded content
